before: The displayed finite-index subgroup is torsion free, so the torsion subgroup injects into the finite quotient. The fixed Tate module is the inverse limit of the local rational2-power torsion groups under multiplication2, which is zero for a finite2-primary group. Any invariant vector in the rational Tate module becomes an invariant integral vector after multiplying by a fixed power of2. Hence it is zero. The quadratic character twist is the Tate module of the actual local quadratic elliptic twist, so the same argument applies.
